content.title: About
content.content: Vegetable curry with rice is a fragrant Indian-inspired dish that combines a variety of vegetables, curry spices, and steamed rice. The meal is rich in vitamins, minerals, and plant‑based protein, making it suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking for a light yet nourishing lunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Curry is not a single ingredient but a blend of spices traditionally including turmeric, cumin, coriander, ginger, and chili.
Vegetable curry is often cooked with coconut milk, giving it a creamy texture and a subtle sweetness.
The dish is popular across Asia and adapted to local tastes, such as adding tofu in Japan or noodles in Thailand.
Traditional Indian rice served with curry is frequently prepared using the "absorption" method so the grains stay separate.
Curry is considered a warming dish, often enjoyed during cooler weather.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The vegetables in the curry (e.g., carrots, broccoli, bell peppers) provide vitamins A, C, and B‑complex, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric and ginger have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties that help protect cells.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and coriander stimulate bile production, aiding fat digestion.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with minimal oil, the dish remains heart‑friendly.

items.title: Plant protein source
items.content: Legumes such as chickpeas or lentils are often added, boosting the protein content.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to turmeric, cumin, or chili; test tolerance before consuming large amounts.

items.title: Heat level
items.content: The dish can be very spicy; those with sensitive stomachs should reduce the amount of chili.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared curry sauces sometimes contain added salt; control salt levels when cooking at home.

items.title: Coconut milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to coconut should substitute with other plant milks.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the vegetable curry hot alongside steamed or boiled rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro, lime wedges, and a sprinkle of toasted seeds (e.g., pumpkin). For a heartier meal, add tofu, chickpeas, or fried tempeh.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stovetop or in the microwave, adding a splash of water or plant milk to restore moisture.
